labels.note: Table 4-1 in Section 4 (Tower and Monopile Properties) lists 'Young's modulus, steel' with symbol E, value '2 00E11' (i.e., 2.00E11), unit Pa. The claim's entity, attribute, value, unit, section, and quote all match the highlighted table row; the value is a stated table entry, so exact (not approximate) is right and basis 'unknown' is acceptable since no basis is stated.

The highlighted region and Figure 8 on the page both show the clothes-dryer scoring rule: 'Reduced points: 100 < % of original weight < 110', exactly matching the claimed value, unit and verbatim quote. The reading is faithful; the only gap is that no section was attributed (it belongs to the Clothes Dryer Subcontest, Figure 8) and basis is marked 'unknown' though it is a stated scoring rule.

The source says the tower height was chosen so the hub reaches 150 m, 'allowing for 30 m of ground (water surface) clearance with 120-m blades.' The 30 m is a blade-tip clearance above the ground/water surface, not a 'depth' of the ground or water; the claim misreads clearance as depth and binds it to a vague entity 'ground.' The quote is truncated right before the key word 'clearance,' which enables the misreading.

A is from Team Capitol DC sheet S-522 (deck footing details); the "2\" X 4\" FRAMING" callout is genuinely on the sheet (in the deck-module connection detail), so the 2x4 framing size is supported. B is from Team Calgary sheet A-202, and the leader actually reads "2x4 CEDAR HANDRAILS" — a guard/handrail, not deck framing. These are different components in two competing designs, so they are not corresponding subjects; treating B's cedar as the material for A's framing (complementary) is wrong — they should be unrelated.

The figure is a Bode plot (magnitude in dB and phase in degrees vs. frequency, 0.01–1 Hz) of the generator speed low-pass filter, and the surrounding text identifies that filter as a recursive, single-pole design whose response is shown for the chosen corner frequency and time step. The about statement matches this subject without quoting numeric parameters; the role correctly reflects the text ('the frequency response of the resulting filter is shown in the Bode plot'); keywords cover the main topics. Type/density is not applicable since this is a figure, not a section.

Figure 2-6 is titled 'Blade: IEA 15MW Offshore Reference Turbine; Section : 0.7' and its legend lists 'Carbon UD' among the materials shown in the blade cross-section at 70% span. The claim's value, condition and verbatim quote match the legend; however, Carbon UD is only one of six legend materials (Medium Density Foam, Glass Triax, Glass Biax, Carbon UD, Glass Uni, Gelcoat), and the others were not extracted.

Figure 9 (§9-2 Cooking) plots 'Points per cooking task' vs 'Weight of vaporized water (oz)': the curve rises and plateaus at the dashed 80 oz line, and the adjacent table states 'Full points: Weight ≥ 80 oz' while the text says all available points are earned at 80.00 oz. The claim that points per cooking task reach their maximum for vaporized water weight ≥ 80 oz is faithful. The 'quote' is a chart-axis description with bracketed annotations rather than a pure verbatim string, and basis 'unknown' understates that this is a scoring rule, but neither undermines the fact.

Figure 2-10(c) plots axial stiffness vs r/R (caption: computed using PreComp) with a 1e10 y-axis scale. The curve starts near ~4.6e10 at the root and falls steeply to ~2.2e10 by r/R≈0.2, so at r/R=0.1 it is roughly ~3e10 N, not 4e10 N; 4e10 corresponds to a nearer-root location. The quote stitches axis labels and inserts "0.1," which is not an x-tick label (ticks are 0.0, 0.2, ...), and the basis is stated in the caption as computed (PreComp), not unknown.

A correctly reads the highlighted Table 7-1 row (wind speed 25.0 m/s) in the NREL 5MW Region-3 blade-pitch sensitivity table, and B correctly reads the IEA 15MW line "10.59 m/s ≤ U ≤ 25 m/s; rated power" (the third of the three listed regions). They are counterparts in two designs both bearing on above-rated/Region-3 wind speed for pitch control: A is a single operating point (the table's top/cut-out value) while B gives the rated-power range, i.e. distinct but compatible information, so "complementary" fits.

The source (Section 8-5, Dishwasher, item d) states verbatim: 'If the dishwasher has a heated drying option, this option shall be disabled.' The entity, attribute, value, condition, quote, and section all match exactly. The only issue is the basis field marked 'unknown' when the text is clearly a requirement ('shall be disabled').

The highlighted region shows the title 'SECTION - EAST MODULE' with the scale '3/8" = 1'-0"' printed directly beneath it, exactly as claimed. The reading is verbatim and correctly bound to the East Module section; the only issue is that a drawing scale is boilerplate with little comparative value.

The figure is a line graph titled 'Scoring function for the Clothes Dryer Subcontest' with x-axis '% of original weight' and y-axis 'Points per clothes drying task', plus a legend defining full/reduced/no point bands. The about statement accurately describes this relationship without citing the specific thresholds (100/110) or point values. Role is empty but nothing incorrect is stated; keywords capture the main topics; the type field is not applicable since this is a figure, not a section.

The highlighted region on sheet A-202 (Exterior Elevations) shows the label 'CEMENT FIBRE BOARD SIDING' on the south elevation, and the quote is verbatim. The material reading is faithful, but the claim is classified as kind 'table' when it is actually a drawing annotation/label on an elevation, not a table.

Sheet A-302 'BUILDING SECTIONS' contains exactly two section drawings: C1 'Section - Centre Module' and A1 'Living Room Section', with labeled rooms (kitchen, bathroom, mechanical room, living rooms), finished-floor and grade-level elevation markers, and centre/west module labels. The about statement matches this content accurately and usefully, naming both sections, the room designations, and the elevation references without quoting dimensions or design decisions. However, the role field is empty, so the item never states why the sheet is included; keywords cover the main topics (sections, modules, floor/grade levels).

In detail A6 (Landscape Footing 18") the 4x4 post sits centered on a 1'-0" wide base; the left dimension string reads 4 1/4" from the left edge of the base to the post face (and 4 1/4" on the right), which is consistent with 4.25 + 3.5 + 4.25 = 12". The quoted value is verbatim and the left offset is correctly read; the explicit dimension is exact, not approximate.

Figure 10's scoring function shows the points line reaching 100 at 0 kWh net electrical energy, and the body text confirms full points are earned for a net electrical energy balance of at least 0 kWh. The value, unit, entity, section, and verbatim caption quote all match; marking it approximate is reasonable for a chart reading (and the text corroborates it exactly). Basis 'unknown' is incomplete—it is a scoring rule/requirement—but not incorrect.
